RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday, the March 9, 2006/Phalguna 18, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; External Affairs; Non-
Conventional Energy Sources; Ocean Development; Overseas Indian Affairs;
Panchayati Raj; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Planning;
Power; Science and Technology; Shipping, Road Transport and Highways;
Space; Statistics and Programme Implementation; Urban Development;
Urban Employment and Poverty Alleviation; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
JNNURM in Mumbai
†*261. SHRI VASANT CHAVAN: Will
the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether funds have been allocated
for damaged buildings in Mumbai under
the Jawahar Lal Nehru National Urban
Renewal Mission (JNNURM);
(b) if so, the amount of funds that have
been allocated under this Mission;
(c) the number of old buildings that
would be renovated under it; and
(d) if not, whether Government are
considering this subject?
Upgradation of coastline ports in
Gujarat
*262. SHRI RAJU PARMAR: Will the
Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that though
Gujarat has 25 per cent of the country's
coastline with many ports and all sections
of the coastal highway along this coast has
not been upgraded to National Highway;
and
(b) if so, the time envisaged for this
upgradation?
Application of advanced technology in
space activities
*263. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) where do we stand in the application
of advanced technology in space activities
in comparison with the developed/
developing countries;
(b) whether our objective to use space
technology as an instrument for socio-
economic development of people has been
achieved;
(c) whether the process of finding out
the natural resources like water, forest,

82
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
minerals, other potentialities of every State
has been completed; and
(d) if so, how many States have used
such information?
Outsourcing services in the process of
issue of visas
*264. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some of the
services in the process of issue of visas in
some countries have been outsourced in
view of huge demand;
(b) if so, the countries and the type of
service outsourced for the purpose;
(c) the other countries where a similar
action is proposed to be taken;
(d) whether enough security
considerations were taken into account
before allowing outsourcing; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Sports potential amongst youth of
NER
†*265. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the boys and
girls of the North-Eastern States have the
potential to become a good sportsperson;
(b) if so, whether there is any scheme
under the consideration to establish a
sports academy in that region with a view
to exploit the sports potential;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Telecast of achievements
in S&T
*266. SHRI DARA SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of SCIENCE AND
TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has tied up
with National Geographic Channel to
produce and telecast a range of programmes
showing the achievements made in different
disciplines of science and technology in
India;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the length of films proposed to be
produced;
(d) the expenditure likely to be incurred
thereon; and
(e) the time by which the said films are
likely to be telecast?
Legislation to regulate MPLADS
*267. SHRI SHANT ARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
STATISTICS AND PROGRAMME
IMPLEMENTATION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
enact a legislation to regulate Members of
Parliament Local Area Development
Scheme in view of the discovery of certain
currupt practices being resorted to; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

83
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Preparation for Commonwealth
Games
†*268. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS
AND SPORTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made
adequate preparations for organizing
Commonwealth Games;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of construction work
carried out so far alongwith the amount
spent by Government?
Availability of drinking water in
Delhi
*269. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the minimum requirement
of drinking water in Delhi is not being
fulfilled;
(b) if so, the details thereof alongwith
the per capita availability of water during
the last one year; and
(c) the steps Government propose to
take to provide adequate safe drinking water
to the residents of Delhi dur

Conventional Energy Sources;  Ocean Development; Overseas Indian Affairs;
Panchayati Raj;  Personnel,  Public Grievances and Pensions;  Planning;
 Power; Science and Technology; Shipping, Road Transport and

 Urban Development; Urban Employment and Poverty

Total number of questions — 155
Atomic Energy Production
1781. PROF. P.J. KURIAN: Will the
PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any plans
to set up more Atomic Energy Plants with
the latest safeguards available in the
international market;
(b) the details of the plans to increase
atomic energy production in the next five
years;
(c) the obstacles in increasing energy
production from atomic energy sources; and
(d) the steps proposed to improve the
sector?
Recommendations of Kirit Parikh
Panel
1782. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that  Kirit Parikh
Panel has recommended that nuclear energy
is critical for long term energy security for
the country;
(b) if so, the details of recommendations
made by the panel; and
(c) whether the country would be short
of indigenous uranium to be used as fuel in
support of a vastly enlarged nuclear power
programme that would be consistent with
the obligation to contribute to the campaign
against global warming?
Thorium as basic Atomic Energy
1783. SHRI E.M. SUDARSANA
NATCHIAPPAN:
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Atomic Energy
Commission has pointed out that thorium,
which is available in abundance in the
country should be the base for the country's
nuclear energy programme and not imported
nuclear fuels; and

403
(b) if so, the decision taken by
Government in this regard?
Captive coal mining blocks
1784. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Coal India
Limited has total 136 captive coal mining
blocks;
(b) the location of these coal mining
blocks, State-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that about 200
million tonnes of coal would be produced
from these blocks;
(d) whether Government have made any
efforts to increase productivity of our coal
mines; and
(e) the steps proposed to set targets
which would increase coal production in
the country?
Coal Mines Provident Fund
Organisation
1785. SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
SHRIMATI BRINDA  KARAT:
Will the Minister of COAL  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Coal Mines Provident
Fund Organisation is paying less rate of
interest than the Employees Provident Fund
Organisation;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons for different rate of
interest payment by the two organisations;
and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to ensure uniformity in the
rate of interest payment?
Arrears to coal workers
1786. SHRIMATI BRINDA  KARAT:
          SHRI CHITTABRATA
MAJUMDAR:
Will the Minister of COAL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
a deep resentment is prevailing among the
coal workers all over the country for non-
payment of arrears of the Seventh Bipartite
Agreement signed last year;
(b) if so, the reasons for the delay in
payment of arrears;
(c) whether the unions in coal industry
have informed the Coal India Ltd. that they
would go on strike if the payment is not
made earlier; and
(d) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to ensure early payment of
arrears?
Disinvestment in Neyveli Lignite
Corporation
1787. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had taken a decision to make disinvestment
of 10 per cent of Government's equity in
Neyveli Lignite Corporation;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government have decided on capacity
expansion of various open cast projects;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Rising coal stocks
1788. SHRIMATI  S.G. INDIRA: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Coal

404
India Ltd. finds itself saddled with rising
coal stocks;
(b) whether it is also a fact that at least
five of its seven coal producing subsidiaries
are carrying an inventory that might be the
highest in a decade; and
(c) if so, the steps taken by CIL to
liquidate this rising stock of coal?
Committee on revision of royalty on
Coal
1789. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of COAL be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Committee that has been
set up to look into the Revision of Royalty
given on coal has submitted its report;
(b) the recommendations made by the
Economic Advisory Council to the Prime
Minister with regard to payment of royalty
on coal at ad-valorem basis or the tonnage
